I am 68 years old. I have been farming since I was 20, and I never went to school — I cannot read or write. But I know my land. My son and daughter-in-law work at the textile factory in town, so it is mostly me and my old man in the fields, with the grandchildren helping after school and on weekends. We have a bit over 10 mu of land. About 7 mu I do wheat then maize, same as my neighbors. The other 3 mu I plant cotton — I cannot do more than that because my back cannot take all that picking, and cotton needs picking three or four times.

The wheat went in last October, same time as always. I used the improved seed my neighbor Wang recommended — it does not fall over easy. Now it is April and the wheat is growing green. I put base fertilizer down when I planted, about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Now I need to topdress with urea. I do about 30 jin of urea per mu, half at green-up and half at jointing. My old man carries the bags and I spread it by hand. I irrigate three times for wheat — spring green-up, jointing, and grain filling. The pump electricity costs too much, but last year I tried to save money and only did two times, and the yield dropped by nearly 100 jin per mu. Never again.

For cotton, I plant in late April after the wheat topdressing is done. I plow those 3 mu and put farmyard manure and some compound fertilizer in the furrows. I bought improved cotton seed from the village supply shop. Cotton is worrying because of the bollworms — I have to spray insecticide two or three times. I irrigate twice if it does not rain. Harvest is the hardest part. I hire women from the village to help pick, and I pay them by the jin.

Maize goes in right after wheat harvest in early June. There is no time — sometimes only four or five days between harvest and planting. I hire the village tractor to chop the wheat straw and plant the maize seeds. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting. If the summer rain is good, I irrigate once at tasseling. If it is dry, twice. Last year the rain was good and I only irrigated once.

Money is always tight. My son sends some home every month, but I cannot spend it all on the farm. Total I spend about 3,000 yuan on seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, and irrigation for the whole year. I use family labor as much as possible. I learned long ago — better to put a little too much fertilizer than too little. Losing a crop means going hungry. I expect about 800 jin per mu for wheat, around 900 jin for maize, and maybe 500 jin of cotton per mu if the worms do not ruin it.
